text:
A: Hello, good evening. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yes. Hello, I'm Claire.
A: Tomasz. Nice to meet you, Claire.
B: You too. You're the last one of mine, I think. Where are you?
A: West London, Hanwell. I'm operations manager for a facilities management company, so office buildings, cleaning, security, maintenance. Six supervisors. Sorry, I always say the job first, my wife tells me off for that.
B: [laughs] It's fine, I'll do the same. Interior design, I've got a studio in Canterbury with a partner. I live in Faversham.
A: Ah, interior design. So you would look at my dining room and hate it, yeah?
B: Well, I can see it. Grey walls. Everyone's got grey walls. It's not your fault, it's the estate agents.
A: [laughs] My wife chose the grey. We bought the house in 2019, and we did a new kitchen last year, very nice, the quartz worktop, the big island.
B: Did you choose the kitchen or did a showroom choose it for you?
A: Er... the showroom, a little bit, to be honest. Is that bad?
B: No, it's normal. It's just that people spend thirty grand and end up with the same kitchen as the neighbours. I'd rather you'd found an old butcher's block at a reclamation yard, but that's me. I'm a bit of a snob about it, I know.
A: Is that okay, what I said? I think you are judging my kitchen. [laughs]
B: I am, a bit. Ignore me. What do you actually like about your job?
A: Er, good question. I think when a client is angry, really angry, and I go to the building and fix it, and at the end they are happy, they shake my hand. I like that. Also, to be honest, I like the title. When I came to London I was cleaning offices at night. Nobody looks at the cleaner. Now the directors copy me in on the emails.
B: That's a good answer. Most people pretend they don't care about the title.
A: I care. Maybe too much. I want to be Head of Operations in three years.
B: Well, at least you know. I've got no ambition at all, really. I cut my hours right down after my divorce, I do twelve hours a week, and my partner does all the invoices. Without her I'd be bankrupt by Christmas.
A: Twelve hours? Wow. I do twelve hours on Monday.
B: Yes, well. I've got two kids, and I'd rather be there when they get home. Do you have kids?
A: One daughter, Zofia, five. She just started reception. Every week the school wants another donation for something, cake sale, trip, a new garden.
B: Oh, that never stops. Mine are fifteen and eleven and I still forget the forms. I saw the crucifix above your door. Do you go to church?
A: Yes, Polish church in Ealing, most Sundays. Zofia was baptised there. You?
B: Christmas and Easter. I like the building and the hymns. The actual beliefs, I'm not so sure. I sort of like the idea of something bigger, though.
A: I think for me it's more the family, the habit. My mum would kill me if I stopped, you—
